messages:
Carla M: heads up — seeing a weird spike in console \"org preview\" rows during the canary. some customers see other orgs' snippets for a few seconds when switching tabs :eyes:
Ben T: ugh, reproducible? steps?
Carla M: yep — repro on prod-canary for me: rapid org switch -> hover on insights -> preview shows rows from previous org for ~2-4s. only in the console UI, backend logs show correct org on the request.
Alice R: can you paste the network/devtools trace? headers/cookies might reveal prefetch key mismatch.
Carla M: pasting snippet:
```
GET /api/insights/preview?org=12345 200 OK
Request headers:
  x-org-id: 12345
  x-prefetch-key: preview:org-12345:user-678
Response payload: preview_rows(org=12345)
After rapid switch -> new request:
GET /api/insights/preview?org=98765 200 OK
Request headers:
  x-org-id: 98765
  x-prefetch-key: preview:org-12345:user-678  <-- still old prefetch key
Response payload: preview_rows(org=12345)  // UI renders this while store hydrates
```
Ben T: looks like prefetch cache key isn't being regenerated on route switch — key includes org but the code path that computes it is gated behind the old route's lifecycle. likely a race where the old in-flight prefetch wins and overwrites the store.
Dave SRE: do we have telemetry showing how often x-prefetch-key != x-org-id? we can query logs to count mismatches.
Carla M: initial grep shows ~0.8% of preview calls in the canary group had mismatched keys in the last 3 hours. mostly under high-nav churn.
Alice R: that explains the UI flash. UI applies the first payload and then later re-hydrates with the correct one. fix options: 1) make prefetch key include request id or route timestamp so old inflight can't be mistaken for fresh, 2) cancel previous prefetches on route change, 3) apply server-side guard: server rejects prefetch payload if X-Prefetch-Key doesn't match current computed key for the incoming x-org-id.
Ben T: we also need to consider quotas + routing: if we change key shape it affects cache hit rates on dedicated pools and may increase upstream load. prefer client-side cancel + lightweight server guard for a quick patch.
Dave SRE: agree — server guard is low-risk: respond 409 if mismatch and let client retry. that keeps metrics clean so quotas don't attribute wrong orgs.
Carla M: can a quick patch be feature-flagged? we should avoid a broad change before we validate impact on cache+dedicated routing.
Ben T: yep — short-lived FF \"prefetch-org-tighten\". I'll send a PR to client to cancel inflight prefetch on route leave + add guard in edge-service behind FF.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout snapshot: infra-canary-42 -> 12% traffic (updated 2m ago).
Alice R: also adding telemetry event: prefetch_key_mismatch with fields [observed_key, expected_key, x-org-id, route] so we can break down by route and customer. keep sample rate at 100% for the next 30m then downsample.
Dave SRE: create a dashboard tile under Console > Isolation > Prefetch Mismatch showing rate, top orgs, and latency delta when mismatch occurs. set an alert at 0.5% sustained over 15m in canary.
Carla M: thanks. can someone take the followups? 1) Ben — PR + FF for client + edge, 2) Alice — telemetry event and temporary high-sample, 3) Dave — dashboard + alert. I'll own the postmortem writeup if we decide to revert/roll-forward.
Ben T: on it. I'll target a small client patch (cancel on route-leave) + edge guard behind FF. will post link to PR in thread. :thumbsup:
Alice R: adding event now, will bump sampling.
Dave SRE: dashboard + alert created (panel id: CON-PRF-324). alert rule linked.
Carla M: temporary mitigation: canary rollback if mismatch > 1% and customer impact observed.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for infra-canary-42 by Ben T (FF toggled off) — ETA 3m.
Ben T: toggled FF off for edge guard while client patch propagates. monitoring.
Carla M: confirm no customer data exfil — this is UI-only preview flash; payloads were served but ACLs on main endpoints were correct. still bad UX and confusing telemetry.
Alice R: noted — we've added a quick sampling of affected customer IDs to the event so success teams can proactively reach out if needed.
Dave SRE: follow-up: we should consider routing policy change to prefer per-org affinity on preview queries to reduce cross-org KV churn. but that's a medium-term perf tradeoff.
Carla M: agree — include that in postmortem recommendations. for now, tracking progress. thx team. :heart:
